name: fleet100_b09
prompt:
One image: a sprite sheet of 9 cars for a 2D top-down city game.

THE BODIES MUST BE SLIMMER. A previous attempt drew most of these cars too wide for their length. Measured against the sizes listed: car 1 about 13% too wide, car 4 10%, car 5 13%, car 6 9%, car 7 11%, car 9 14%. Draw every body to its listed proportion, its flanks straight and close together; leave the extra room in each grid place empty rather than filling it with a wider car.

Style: match the attached picture's art style exactly — outline weight, shading, highlights, level of detail, pixel size.

View: straight down from above, orthographic. No perspective, no side of the body showing, no ground, no shadow.

Layout: a 3×3 grid, the cars in the order listed, left to right and top to bottom. Each car lies horizontally with its nose to the right, centred in its place, with empty space round it. One shared scale for all.

Every car:
- Its length and width as listed, in that proportion, with straight flanks. Narrow cars stay narrow: leave spare room empty rather than draw a car wider.
- Mirror-symmetric about its long centre line, with two small side mirrors just ahead of the windscreen.
- Roof on. No tyres or wheels (the game draws them), no people, no text, logos, badges or licence plates.

Background: fully transparent outside the cars — no colour, no glow or halo, no shadow. Each car's edge ends sharply.

The cars in the picture only show the style: draw the cars listed, in their own colours.
- Lamps switched off (unlit glass, no glow). Front corner: a headlamp and, beside it, a separate amber indicator. Rear corner: three separate small lenses side by side, each in its own thin dark frame, as distinct as the front's — red tail and brake lamp outermost, amber indicator next, white reversing lamp innermost. The rear indicator is the same amber as the front one and as large, plainly not red. Never one merged red cluster, never a light bar across the car.
- Condition shows only in the paint (faded colour, rust spots, a panel in another shade); the body outline is whole.

Cars, body length × width without mirrors, and what each is:
1. 4.77 × 1.74 m (2.74× longer than wide), nearly square corners — 1990s German boxy executive estate car, worn: dull silver paint, rust spots on the tailgate, long flat bonnet, long roof with roof rails to an upright tailgate, wide rectangular headlamps, tall tail lamps split into red, amber and white sections. About 13% too wide last time: draw it narrow.
